# Deferred Token Response

> Deferred Token Response (DTR) is an OAuth extension that lets an authorization server return a
> deferral_code instead of an access token when a decision needs more time, and lets the client
> poll the token endpoint until it resolves.

DTR adds a defined way to keep an authorization decision pending: a token request normally ends
with a token response or an error, but the authorization server decides per-request whether it
needs to wait — the same client can get an immediate token for one request and a deferred
response for another. A request might wait on a fraud reviewer, a document owner's approval, an
agent-authorization check, or a long-running policy/identity check.

## Mechanism

1. The client opts in by including `completion_mode=deferred` in its token request.
2. The server defers the decision, returning `authorization_pending`, a `deferral_code`, an
   expiry, and a minimum polling interval — no access token is issued yet.
3. The client polls the token endpoint with the deferral code at the permitted interval. The
   server reports whether the request is still pending, needs external interaction
   (`interaction_required`), or should back off (`slow_down`).
4. The request resolves: approval returns the token response; denial or expiry
   (`access_denied`/`expired_token`) ends the attempt without a token.

## Docs

- [Homepage](https://deferred-token-response.dev/): protocol overview, interactive scenario
  walkthroughs, OAuth vocabulary, and a full wire-level request/response reference.
- [IETF Draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-gerber-oauth-deferred-token-response/): the
  full specification.
- [GitHub — spec](https://github.com/maxwellgerber/deferred-token-response): specification source
  and issue tracker.
- [Live demo](https://demo.deferred-token-response.dev/): a real OAuth client sandbox against a
  real (demo) authorization server, three scenarios (identity-assertion interaction, Rich
  Authorization Requests, fraud review after user consent).
